rationale: Central-bank MIPS/RTGS infrastructure page: recurring source of payments-infrastructure programme and vendor signals; failed check is soft only.
Government session decisions are a durable first-record stream for funded payments/fiscalisation programmes.
Official Gazette is authoritative and high-value but access_status unknown and URL unverified; recheck reachability/licence before approving.
Chamber legislation tracker publishes draft payment/e-invoicing rules plus industry reaction on a continuing basis.
Watchdog's institution/portal directory is best mined once for source leads; ongoing ENER reports are marginal to vendor intel.
State fund procurement store largely mirrors BJN; redundant unless BJN coverage proves incomplete.
Commercial e-invoicing vendor explainers reveal implementation detail and vendor positioning; low credibility but high lead value.
State/mainstream news agencies are a continuous feed carrying MoF, UJP and NBRM payments statements early.
UNDP country hub publishes recurring digital-payments/DPI project reporting naming government counterparts.
Single trade-press article on the Mastercard/Evrotrust digital-ID deal — strong evidence artifact, not a standalone MK monitoring feed.
State Audit Office report repository names IT/payment suppliers, contract values and irregularities; hard adversarial vendor evidence.
NBRM audit sub-section of dzr.mk; covered by monitoring the parent report repository.
Planned-audit register gives months of early warning on which procurement files become public.
DZR annual reports are a subsection of the same domain already monitored via the report repository.
Competition decision register reasons publicly on interchange, acquiring and dominance cases naming banks and PSPs.
Infringement/fine register names sanctioned firms and exposes market-structure disputes.
Merger notifications disclose bank/payment-firm ownership changes ahead of commercial announcement.
Court-review listing is a sibling section of the KZK decisions area already covered.
KZK annual reports are a low-frequency subsection of the same monitored domain.
Supervision hub is the entry point to PSP licensing and supervisory measures; public and allowed.
Supervisory decision register exposes licences, consents and new payment/e-money entrants.
Anti-corruption commission cases name contracts, entities and officials in public-sector IT/payment procurement.
DPA inspections and sanctions reveal processors and outsourced vendors handling bank/PSP customer data.
Consumer body's financial-services desk surfaces recurring complaint patterns on cards, fees and e-payments.
Authoritative e-money institution register — definitive roster of non-bank wallet challengers and new entrants.
Hub page linking the individual PSP registers; mine once to snowball into the registers themselves.
Register of licensed fast money transfer providers maps the remittance channel and bank partners.
